lessons.lesson: Promote and compare the exact validated Git tree, not only a branch label or commit title. If production already contains the exact validated tree, avoid a duplicate deployment.

A stale release branch can carry an older GitHub Actions workflow with weaker gates. Production deployment policy must not depend on an obsolete workflow copy living on the release branch. Prefer a centrally trusted or reusable deployment workflow whose gates are current.

Keep candidate CI, deployment, and live functional proof as separate states. Green full-candidate-ci is necessary but is not a deployment; deployment success is not proof that the Professor UI rendered correctly.

npm ci succeeding is not a security approval. Run an explicit runtime dependency security gate, syntax checks and the full test suite. Distinguish runtime dependency risk from development/tooling findings while keeping the latter visible for maintenance.

After deployment, query the live Worker and record concrete evidence. Teacher Bridge status, pending, work and bridge.txt must answer successfully; UI routes such as /professor should also get an explicit HTML/render smoke when tooling permits.

Never write recurring Teacher transport metadata onto the executable candidate branch. Keep review traffic on teacher-bridge/runtime so teaching metadata cannot invalidate the exact candidate SHA under review.
Do not fabricate a TEACHER_REPLY when no matching runtime request is pending. A lesson should enter persistent Mentor/Learning memory only through a supported, correlated and verifiable path.
Keep the candidate SHA, tree SHA, release/deploy run and Cloudflare version together as deployment provenance so later audits can prove what code was actually published.

observed_anomalies: The production run that published the validated tree used an older release-branch workflow and did not itself rerun the modern audit/check/test gates.

npm ci in that production run reported three high-severity findings; the validated candidate separately passed npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high, so the runtime dependency gate passed while development/tooling findings remain maintenance debt.

The public Teacher Bridge was healthy after deployment but reported pending_count=0 and mutation_allowed=false, so this handoff is transport metadata and is not falsely presented as already ingested into D1 Mentor memory.
recommended_follow_up: Make production deployment call a trusted central/reusable workflow so stale release branches cannot weaken gates.
Add a live smoke for GET /professor that validates HTTP status, content type and a stable Professor-page marker after each production deploy.
Add a supported authenticated/correlated Professor-experience ingestion path that converts validated handoffs into mentor_lessons without requiring a fake pending Teacher request.
Keep exact-tree duplicate-deployment detection before promotion.

learning_status.reason: No pending correlated Teacher request and the public Teacher Bridge is read-only.
